newsitem.title: CHINA: China has "very good" chance of joining WTO-Dunkel.
newsitem.headline: China has "very good" chance of joining WTO-Dunkel.

text.p: China has a "very good" chance of joining the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in the near future, the former director-general of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), Arthur Dunkel, said on Tuesday.

"My opinion is that the prospects are good, very good," Dunkel told reporters at a news conference. "But I have also said that saying the prospects are very good, I never took a bet in terms of the timing."
Beijing and members of the world trade body must first resolve serious questions before China can join the WTO, he said.
Difficulties include a need for progress in the service industry sector, protection of intellectual property rights and improvement of market access.
China has been seeking to join the WTO, and its predecessor the GATT, for a number of years.
Dunkel said negotiations were now focused on the number of years of transition China will be allowed to meet certain WTO obligations after entrance.

Beijing has sought to enter the WTO on the more favourable conditions accorded to developing countries, but many nations have said its economy is too big for such treatment and that it should be admitted only on developed country terms.
"I think that the negotiations have reached the point where the criteria are losing importance," Dunkel said.

Dunkel was asked about suggestions from some U.S. officials that agreement could be reached on China's WTO entry before a meeting of President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin, tentatively planned for later this year.
But he said such deadlines have been missed before.
"You can't go quicker than the wind when you negotiate very serious problems," he said.
